slot.brief: A charged particle enters at angle to a uniform B field; find pitch and radius of helical path, and how pitch changes if speed/angle/B is altered.

stem: The same charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field at $30^\circ$ to the field with speed $v$ and field magnitude $B$. In a second case its speed is $2v$, its angle to the field is $60^\circ$, and the field magnitude is $2B$. What are the ratios of second-case to first-case pitch and radius, respectively?

verdicts.working: Pitch is proportional to v cosθ/B, so the ratio is (2 cos60°/2)/(cos30°) = 1/√3. Radius is proportional to v sinθ/B, so the ratio is (2 sin60°/2)/(sin30°) = √3.

working:
$p=\dfrac{2\pi m v\cos\theta}{|q|B}$, $r=\dfrac{m v\sin\theta}{|q|B}$. $\dfrac{p_2}{p_1}=\dfrac{2\cos60^\circ}{2\cos30^\circ}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$; $\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}=\dfrac{2\sin60^\circ}{2\sin30^\circ}=\sqrt3$.

Independent check: Pitch is proportional to v cosθ/B, so the ratio is (2 cos60°/2)/(cos30°) = 1/√3. Radius is proportional to v sinθ/B, so the ratio is (2 sin60°/2)/(sin30°) = √3.
solution:
For helical motion, $p=\dfrac{2\pi m v\cos\theta}{|q|B}$ and $r=\dfrac{m v\sin\theta}{|q|B}$.
$$\frac{p_2}{p_1}=\frac{2\cos60^\circ}{2\cos30^\circ}=\frac{1}{\sqrt3},\qquad \frac{r_2}{r_1}=\frac{2\sin60^\circ}{2\sin30^\circ}=\sqrt3$$
